provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus ('quaesumus Domine'); 1962 sets 'quaesumus, Domine'; 1862 sets no comma after atque; 1962 sets 'atque, a peccatorum'; CONCLUSION: 1862 prints the short cue 'Per Dominum.'; 1962 prints 'Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.' This is the largest single difference in the lane. It is the standard conclusion formula at a different length, not a different petition; the 1604 sits between the two at 'Per Dominum nostrum.'; 1862 ornamental initial and two words are damaged by the recogniser ('pvlleces', 'hi)6mine', 'imjue'); scan artefacts, not readings. Corroboration: 1604 at lines 15328-15336 ('T\Reces noftras, quæfumus Domine, clementer exaudi: atque a peccatorum vinculis abfolutos, ab omni nos aduerfitate cuftodi. Per Dominum noftrum.') -- independently confirms the petition word for word and, like the 1862, omits the comma after atque. 1570 not located: that OCR's Quinquagesima Collect does not appear in reading order between the Sexagesima Gospel and the Quinquagesima Epistle, which is scrambling in the 1570 text layer and NOT a finding about the 1570 book. Corroboration only..

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 places the comma after quaesumus rather than after Domine ('Domine quaesumus,'); 1962 sets 'Domine, quaesumus,'; 1862 sets no comma after et; 1962 sets 'et, ad sacrificium'; 1862 conclusion is 'Per Dominum.'; 1962 extends it to 'Per Dominum nostrum.'; TEXT-LAYER DAMAGE, not a difference: the 1862 recogniser drops 'deli-' at the end of line 19052, leaving 'emundet nostra' / 'cta:'. The word cannot be anything but delicta, and both the 1570 and the 1604 print delicta at this place, but I could not read it in the 1862 itself. Corroboration: 1604 at lines 15397-15405 ('T Aec hoftia, Domine quæfumus, emundet noftra delicta: & ad facrificium celebrandum, fubditorum tibi corpora, mentefq. fanctificet. Per Dominum.') -- prints delicta, and like the 1862 has no comma after et; unlike either, it sets a comma after corpora. 1570 at lines 14859-14862 ('[Hae]c hoftia, dñe q̃s, emüdct [nof]tra delicta: [et] facrificiu celebrãdi fübditor tibi co:po:a metesq5 fãctificet. Per.') -- also prints delicta. Both are degraded-latin and are corroboration only; they are what makes me confident the 1862's lost fragment is delicta, but they are not the 1862.. Recorded limitation: THE ONE WEAK ENTRY IN THIS LANE, and the reason is a single word. Everything else here is pointing and the conclusion. But 'delicta' is not readable in the tracked public-domain witness at this locus: the 1862 text layer lost the fragment at a column line-break. I could not settle it on the 1862 page image because that book's image payloads are not installed in this checkout -- only artifact.toml manifests exist for ia-facsimile-pdf-363d6fc3 and ia-original-page-images-tar-fd220b49, and the registered per-leaf artifacts (leaves 221, 303, 347-349, 700-701, 706, 721-725) do not include the leaf for printed p. 51, which by the recorded leaf = printed + 85 rule would be leaf 136. If the applying agent wants this at high confidence, the cheap fix is to acquire and read 1862 leaf 136; short of that the word rests on inference plus the 1570 and the 1604, and I have not rounded that up.
